name: FileRow
label: File row
description: One file in a list: its type mark, its name as a link or a button, a line of detail and controls at the end.

props.name: name
props.description: The file's name with its extension (`Q3 report.pdf`), which also picks its type mark.

props.name: mimeType
props.description: The file's MIME type, when its name has no telling extension.

props.name: kind
props.description: The file's kind, when neither its name nor its MIME type says it.
props.defaultExpression: picked from the name and the MIME type

props.name: typeLabel
props.description: The type mark's lettering, in place of the one derived from the name.

props.name: meta
props.description: A quiet second line: the size, who added it, when.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the name a link to the file or its preview page.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Makes the name a button that opens the file in place, such as in a DocumentViewer dialog. `href` wins when both are set.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls at the row's end: a download, a share, a menu.

props.name: size
props.description: Row density: `compact` for a list in a side panel.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component the name's link renders with, such as Next.js's `Link`, so
it navigates through the app's router; a plain `<a>` when unset. This
component can render on the server, so it never reads a LinkProvider:
pass the prop even under one.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

keys.note: The name is a native link or button and the actions passed in are native controls, reached with Tab.

alternatives.name: AttachmentTile
alternatives.when: the file sits on a chat message or in a composer, shown as a square
